messages:
maya: Heads-up 1:30 UTC I'm opening a docs PR to add 'resume pagination' examples for streaming and non-streaming flows. Need short, copy-pasteable snippets for Py/TS/Go. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4892

sam: Ack. I'll take TS. Want to show both cursor resume and offset-wrapping behavior?

maya: Prefer opaque token caveat + resume snippet that shows state checkpointing. No offsets in examples.

alex: I'll do Python. Should we include a tiny test harness example for the gallery so maintainers can run locally?

maya: Yes please, a 3-line harness that simulates intermittent failures and resumes using stored token.

jia: I'll craft the Go snippet. Keep it idiomatic: show context + Cancel handling and simple retry loop.

nate: Can the snippets avoid external deps where possible? For backoff we can use small inline retry helpers instead of importing backoff libs.

amaya: (typo) meant maya: @nate good call. Inline retry helper for docs is better.

sam: Draft TS snippet (short):

```ts
// resume pagination (async iterator)
const pageStream = client.embeddings.stream({ model: 'embed-1', input: '...' })
let token = null
for await (const page of pageStream) {
  // process page.items
  token = page.next_cursor
  // persist token to resume later
}

// resume later: pass cursor token
const resumed = client.embeddings.list({ cursor: token })
for await (const item of resumed) { console.log(item) }
```

sam: Note: used property `next_cursor` in examples to be explicit but we'll add a note that field names may change across SDKs.

alex: Python draft (blocking + async resume):

```python
# blocking (sync) resume example
cursor = None
while True:
    resp = client.embeddings.list(model="embed-1", cursor=cursor)
    for it in resp.items:
        print(it.vector[:3])
    cursor = resp.next_cursor
    if not cursor:
        break

# async streaming resume (compact)
async def run_resume():
    token = load_token()  # app-specific persistent store
    async for page in client.embeddings.stream(model="embed-1", cursor=token):
        process(page.items)
        save_token(page.next_cursor)
```

alex: I'll push this with a tiny harness that simulates a raised exception after first page and shows resume.

jia: Go snippet (recv + resume):

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()
var cursor string
for {
  resp, err := client.Embeddings.List(ctx, &api.ListEmbeddingsRequest{Model: "embed-1", Cursor: cursor})
  if err != nil { log.Fatalf("list failed: %v", err) }
  for _, it := range resp.Items { fmt.Println(it.Vector[:3]) }
  if resp.NextCursor == "" { break }
  cursor = resp.NextCursor
}
```

jia: For streaming resume with Recv() loop I'll add a short example too. Will avoid heavy backoff libs per earlier note.

nate: Quick review note: docs should warn that tokens are opaque and short-lived (may be invalidated on model change/quantization). Also call out that resumed streams may produce duplicates; apps should be idempotent.

maya: Add both those caveats. Also add a tiny bullet about size limits on token size and retention policy (link to compliance doc).

sam: CI: snippet-lint job will check code fence languages. I'll run it after I push TS tweaks.

docs-bot: PR #4892 opened by maya: docs/examples: add resume-pagination snippets (py/ts/go). Status: open.

alex: Pushed Python + harness. Harness is 20 lines max, uses simple file to store token.

sam: Pushed TS tweaks: used camelCase `nextCursor` to align with SDK naming; added semicolons.

jia: Pushed Go streaming resume and a note about context cancellation.

docs-bot: CI started: docs-build, snippets-lint.

ci: snippets-lint failed: detected `next_cursor` vs `nextCursor` mismatch across files.

maya: Ok I'll standardize examples to say "next_cursor (SDK name may vary)" in the code comments and keep the code using the idiomatic SDK name per language. That should placate lint.

maya: Updated PR description with checklist: [x] py sync + async resume, [x] ts async + resume example, [x] go list + stream resume, [x] caveats and links. Asking for final LGTM.

sam: LGTM from TS side.

alex: LGTM python. Pulled runtime behavior locally, resume worked as documented.

jia: LGTM go.

docs-bot: PR #4892 merged by maya. Release note: docs/examples: resume pagination + streaming snippets (py/ts/go); added caveats on opaque tokens and duplicate handling. :shipit:

maya: Great work, thanks all. I'll open a follow-up to instrument a tiny integration test for resume flows in the snippets repo.
